subject: Edge deployment — consumption split, platform fee amortization, and support tier clarification
messages:
From: Omar Castillo <omar.castillo@horizonedge.ai>
To: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@horizonedge.ai>
Date: Sun, 13 Sep 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Clarify on-prem commercial structure and SSO impact

Hi Priya,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team was impressed with the latency and the KV-cache behavior. We have two procurement questions that are blocking our internal eval:

1) Platform fee amortization: Our finance team prefers a model where the platform fee can be amortized quarterly rather than billed as a single upfront entitlement. Is that supported for on-prem / VPC installs? If not, what flexibility do you have for a 12-month amortization schedule?

2) Consumption split for hybrid usage: We expect ~70% on-prem (edge nodes) and 30% hosted queries during peak. Can you confirm whether the node-based license + metered hosted calls approach we discussed will keep us within the same SLA and support tier, or will that trigger additional entitlements?

3) Support tiers & SSO: We need 24x5 on-call and SAML SSO support from day one. Does SSO onboarding sit in the implementation scope or in the support retainer? Any runbook or checklist you can share would be helpful.

We have a draft PO ready but need the above clarified before routing for signature. Also, if you could point us to a sample SOW and a one-pager on support tiers, that would accelerate things on our end.

Appreciate it — can loop in procurement folks if needed.

Best,
Omar
Director of Infrastructure, HorizonEdge

--
HorizonEdge (www.horizonedge.ai)
From: Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
To: Omar Castillo <omar.castillo@horizonedge.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Sep 2026 09:40:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem commercial structure and SSO impact

Hi Omar — thanks for the clear list. Short answers up top and an attached starter SOW + support matrix.

- Platform fee amortization: We can amortize the platform fee over 12 months (quarterly invoices). For amortization we ask for a minimum 12-month commitment on the Starter/Enterprise bundle; the contract will note the amortization schedule.

- Consumption split: Your proposed mix (70% node-based on-prem, 30% hosted) is supported without moving you out of the agreed support tier, provided the combined peak qps stays within the committed capacity in the SOW. If the hosted portion exceeds a burst threshold (we'll include thresholds in the SOW), auto-burst will apply at metered rates.

- SSO & onboarding: SSO onboarding is part of the implementation work (SOW), but ongoing SAML maintenance falls under the Bronze/Silver/Gold support tiers (we've attached the tier table). For 24x5 on-call we recommend the Gold retainer.

Attachments: HorizonEdge_SOW_Draft_v0.2.pdf, Support_Tiers_Table.xlsx

Next steps I'd propose:
1) I send a revised SOW that explicitly calls out amortization dates and the burst thresholds.
2) Ben (cc'd) will propose a limited implementation credit to help with SSO/agent onboarding cost.

If that sounds OK, we'll turn the SOW into a redline-friendly doc for your procurement.

Cheers,
Priya Natarajan
Account Lead, Redwood Inference
priya_natarajan@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

--
Attachment stubs: HorizonEdge_SOW_Draft_v0.2.pdf (pdf), Support_Tiers_Table.xlsx (spreadsheet)
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
To: Omar Castillo <omar.castillo@horizonedge.ai>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Avery Johnson <avery_johnson@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Sep 2026 08:17:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem commercial structure and SSO impact

Omar — looping in commercial details so procurement has numbers to work with. Priya summarized well; a few specifics from our side:

- Implementation credit: We can extend a one-time implementation credit equal to 15% of the first-year platform fee to offset onboarding (covers SSO agent & initial ops runbook). Credit applies if contract signed within 45 days.

- Platform fee amortization: We will accept quarterly invoices for the amortized platform fee. To make this operational, the contract will specify an amortization schedule and an early-termination true-up (standard).

- Billing & PO: We accept standard PO referencing Redwood Master Services Agreement. Invoices will be sent to the billing contact in your PO; net-30 preferred.

- Discount mechanics: 12-month term, 10% off the platform fee for the first year (stackable with the implementation credit). We will include an appendix with examples showing seat/node vs metered hosted cost for the 70/30 split.

Attached: Discount_Term_Sheet.pdf (summary of what the 10% and 15% credit look like on a sample bill).

If you want an escalated pricing counter (e.g., larger commit in exchange for deeper discount), call me and we can model it quickly.

Thanks — Ben
Ben Carter
VP, Revenue Operations | Redwood Inference
ben_carter@redwood.com | +1 650-555-0199

--
Attachment stub: Discount_Term_Sheet.pdf (pdf)
From: Omar Castillo <omar.castillo@horizonedge.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya_natarajan@redwood.com>
Cc: Lena Park <lena.park@horizonedge.ai>
Date: Wed, 15 Sep 2026 10:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Clarify on-prem commercial structure and SSO impact

Ben/Priya — this is helpful, thanks. A couple of quick procurement asks so we can move to PO: 

- Please send a short checklist for procurement (SOC2 attestation, ATO/network contacts, invoice remit details, PO language example).
- We'll accept the 12-month amortization and the 10% first-year discount + 15% implementation credit, provided the credit is itemized on the first invoice.
- Can you also add a short example appendix in the SOW that shows cost delta between node-licensed vs node + 30% hosted metered at 1M tokens/day? That will make it trivial for our finance team to sign.

If you can drop the updated SOW + the procurement checklist today or tomorrow, we'll route PO by end of week.

Appreciate the responsiveness — we want to move fast on this.

Best,
Omar
Director of Infrastructure, HorizonEdge

--
